title: Comfort proportionate to both people’s energy

captions.energy: Keeping familiar comfort at any cost
captions.emotions: Feeling peace through a suitable measure

meaning: Your domestic support becomes calmer when familiar convenience occupies a proportionate place and help accounts for both people’s capacities.
text: A comfortable home may sustain your hope that everyday life can become easier. The Star in the physical position of Muladhara appears through actions genuinely helping both. The Devil in energy tends to retain familiar comfort regardless of its cost. Temperance in emotions wants peace through a suitable measure. Something pleasant becomes a source of strain: you try to preserve everything familiar although inwardly you already need another combination of care, time and free space.

Suppose you like keeping many plants at home. They bring rooms to life, but care and rearrangement occupy entire weekends; a request for fewer pots sounds like rejection of comfort. **A suitable measure preserves pleasure without requiring unlimited maintenance.** Beauty and workload can be acknowledged together: domestic support is not measured by plant numbers, and both people’s peace also belongs to the purpose for which you arrange the space. Fewer obligations need not make the room uncared for.

The difficulty is hoping that one new care system will make relinquishing anything unnecessary forever. Seeking relief merely retains the previous volume of obligations. Support grows when measure is determined by actual life rather than fear of losing the familiar. Different contributions can be coordinated, but agreement must let both name a limit without making familiar comfort a compulsory test of love for your shared home.
